intro.TrustedMarkup:
A regular expression that searches, counts and replaces.

=~ only answers whether a whole string matches a constant pattern. The walk is Vyrn, not a builtin, so every engine runs one source and agrees on offsets and counts.

The language is std/regex.syntax, the one =~ reads, and a pattern means what it means there: . is any character but and . \d, \w, \s and \h are shorthands, their capitals negate them, and \N is any character but . , , , , \v, \a, \e and \cX are control characters, and \xHH, \x{H..}, \uHHHH, \u{H..} and \o{O..} are code points. \R is a line break, \Q quotes the text up to \E or the end, and a backslash before ASCII punctuation makes it literal. Every other escape is refused. {m,n} repeats a term m to n times, each count at most 255, and a ? after a repeat or a count makes it lazy. (?:..) groups without a name, (?<n>..), (?P<n>..) and (?'n'..) name a group, and (?#..) is a comment. The flags i (ASCII case folding), s (. takes and ) and m hold for the rest of a group after (?ims-ims), or inside (?ims-ims:..), and the empty pattern matches the empty string. A pattern with no backreference is a Thompson NFA with no backtracking, so the time is linear in the pattern size times the input. A search runs it as two lazy DFAs, one forward to a match's end and one back to its start: one table read per byte.

\1 to \99, \gN and \g{N} refer to a group by number, \g{-N} to the Nth group opened before it, and \k<n>, \k'n', \k{n} and (?P=n) by name. A backreference matches the text its group spans, or the empty string where the group has not closed or took no part; under i it folds ASCII case. A reference to a group the pattern does not have is refused. (?>..) is an atomic group, which keeps the first way its body matches, and a + after a repeat or a count makes it possessive, an atomic group around it. A search of a pattern with a backreference, an atomic group or a possessive repeat backtracks from each offset in turn, which takes time exponential in the pattern in the worst case, so one call of find, countMatches, replaceAll or captures takes at most 1000000 steps and 1000 more per byte of the haystack, and past them it traps with a backtracking pattern ran past its step budget of N steps. A repeat that comes back to its loop at the offset it left it ends there, as a thread the NFA drops.

(?=..), (?!..), (?<=..) and (?<!..) look ahead and behind, nested to any depth, and see the whole text, before from too. ^ and $ are the text's ends, or a line's under m; \A and \z are the text's ends, and \Z is the end or a final . is a word boundary and \B any other position, \< and {start} a word's start, \> and {end} its end, and {start-half} and {end-half} the side of each that is no word character. A search of a pattern with an assertion first runs one pass per lookaround body over the text, and then the NFA, not the lazy DFAs: the time stays linear. A capturing group inside a lookaround is refused.

captures gives a match's groups, numbered from 1 in the order of their (; (?:..) and (?i:..) do not count. capture and named read one.

Leftmost-first, as Perl, PCRE and RE2 match: of the matches that start leftmost, the one the pattern prefers, so an earlier alternative wins, a greedy repeat takes as much as it can and a lazy one as little. a|ab against ab matches a.

A class is a set of code points: it unites its members, ranges, POSIX classes such as [:alpha:] and nested classes, and &&, -- and ~~ intersect, subtract and take the symmetric difference of the unions beside them. A literal, a class and . each match one whole character, so offsets are bytes and every match starts and ends on a character boundary.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type Regex = { fwd: Program, rev: Program, // The name of group `k` at `k - 1`, or "" for a group with none. names: Array<String>, // Each lookaround body, inner ones before the bodies that hold them. looks: Array<Look>, // Whether the pattern holds a backreference, an atomic group or a possessive // repeat. backtrack: Bool, }

prose.TrustedMarkup: A compiled pattern: fwd is the pattern after a loop over any byte, so a forward pass finds where the leftmost match ends, and rev, its reverse, reads that match back to its start. A pattern with a backreference is searched by backtracking over fwd, and its rev serves only its regular lookahead bodies.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type Match = { at: Int64, end: Int64 }

prose.TrustedMarkup: One match: a half-open byte range of the haystack.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn compile(pattern: String) -> Result<Regex, String>

prose.TrustedMarkup: Compiles pattern, or says what is wrong with it. Compile once and search often: the whole cost of a pattern is paid here.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn matchesWhole(hay: String, pattern: String) -> Bool

prose.TrustedMarkup:
Whether all of hay matches pattern, which the compiler has checked: =~ over a pattern only the backtracking search matches calls it. It traps past the step budget, as a search does.

ponytail: compiles the pattern on every call. A memo in module state costs every search of this module 22% more fuel (regexredux, 2026-11-28); a memo the emitter owns, one slot per pattern, if a program matches often.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn find(re: Regex, hay: String, from: Int64) -> Option<Match>

prose.TrustedMarkup: The first match at or after from, or None. It reads hay from from to the match's end, and back to its start.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn countMatches(re: Regex, hay: String) -> Int64

prose.TrustedMarkup: How many non-overlapping matches re has in hay: aa in aaa is one. An empty match advances by one byte.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn replaceAll(re: Regex, hay: String, with: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: hay with every non-overlapping match replaced by with, taken literally: $1 is two characters, not a group.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type Captures = { whole: Match, // The offsets group `k` starts and ends at, at `2 * k - 2` and `2 * k - 1`, or // -1 for a group that took no part. A group in a repeat spans its last turn. spans: Array<Int64>, }

prose.TrustedMarkup: A match and the span of each group of its pattern that took part in it.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn captures(re: Regex, hay: String, from: Int64) -> Option<Captures>

prose.TrustedMarkup: The first match at or after from and its groups, or None. The groups cost a Thompson simulation over the match alone; a backtracking search has them.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn capture(c: Captures, k: Int64) -> Option<Match>

prose.TrustedMarkup: Group k of c: the whole match for 0, or None for a group that took no part or that the pattern does not have.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn named(re: Regex, c: Captures, name: String) -> Option<Match>
